name: Grainient
rationale: Clean-room implementation from the one-line effect description only; no upstream source was read. The drifting gradient is pure CSS and the grain is a 2D canvas drawn once per size, so it replaces the WebGL original with no dependency and no animation loop.

intensity.description: Opacity of the gradient layer over the base.

speed.description: Seconds per drift pass (the drift alternates).

grain.description: Opacity of the grain layer; 0 skips the canvas.

grainSize.description: Size of one grain speck, in CSS px.

animate.description: Let the gradient drift slowly; false keeps it still.

a11y: The gradient is a pseudo-element and the grain canvas is aria-hidden with pointer-events none, so neither is announced, focusable or able to intercept clicks.
Content inside the host stays in normal flow above both layers; intensity caps the gradient so text over it can keep 4.5:1 contrast on the base colour.
Reduced motion stops the drift entirely; the grain is never animated, so nothing flickers.
Forced-colors mode removes the gradient and grain and leaves the system background.
